Package com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.application.mfa

package com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.application.mfa
Use cases of the multi-factor framework: security events, second-factor lockout and trusted devices.
  • Class
    Description
    CheckSecondFactorLockoutUseCase
    Use case that tells whether the second factor of a user is locked after too many failed attempts.
    CleanExpiredTrustedDevicesUseCase
    Use case that deletes the trusted devices that have expired, since they can never be used again.
    CreatedTrustedDevice
    A trusted device just created, with the signed cookie value that is only available now.
    CreateTrustedDeviceUseCase
    Use case that trusts the browser of a user for some days so it skips the second factor.
    FindTrustedDeviceUseCase
    Use case that finds the usable (not revoked, not expired) trusted device of a user from the value of the cookie.
    HasConfirmedSecondFactorUseCase
    Use case that tells whether a user has confirmed any second factor, asking every SecondFactorEnrolmentQuery bean.
    IsClientMfaRequiredUseCase
    Use case that tells whether a client makes multi-factor authentication mandatory for every user signing in through it (ClientRegistration.mfaRequired()).
    IsUserMfaRequiredUseCase
    Use case that tells whether the account of a user requires a second factor, whatever the client being served: when an administrator forced it (users.mfa_required) or when the user has confirmed a second factor (asked to HasConfirmedSecondFactorUseCase), since a factor the user enrolled must protect every sign-in.
    ListTrustedDevicesUseCase
    Use case that lists the trusted devices of a user that have not expired.
    MfaConfiguration
    Exposes the domain collaborators of the multi-factor use cases as beans, so no use case creates them and a deployment (or a test) can replace any of them, and binds the MfaProperties.
    MfaProperties
    Multi-factor settings, bound once from authserver.mfa.* and injected wherever one of them is needed (the use cases of this module and the step-up guard of the API).
    RecordSecurityEventUseCase
    Use case that records a security event (login, second factor, lockout, trusted device) in the audit log.
    RegisterSecondFactorFailureUseCase
    Use case that counts a failed second-factor attempt and locks the second factor of the user once authserver.mfa.max-failed-attempts consecutive failures are reached.
    ResetSecondFactorFailuresUseCase
    Use case that clears the failed second-factor attempts of a user, after a successful verification.
    RevokeTrustedDeviceUseCase
    Use case that revokes a trusted device of a user, so it asks for the second factor again.
    SecondFactorEnrolmentQuery
    Extension point that tells whether a user has confirmed one kind of second factor.
    TrustedDeviceTokens
    Creates the random tokens that identify a trusted device and hashes them, so only the SHA-256 hash is ever stored.
